newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati questioned again by police.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati questioned again by police.

text.p: Indonesian police completed questioning ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri on Monday over the organisation of a political rally at her home in January, her lawyers said.
Megawati, daughter of the late founding president Sukarno, was questioned at the South Jakarta Police Headquarters for about an hour and a half, they said.
It was the second time she had been questioned in connection with the meeting, which police said was illegal because authorities were not informed in advance.
"The questioning was only for one-and-a-half hours. It is now finished," lawyer R.O. Tambunan told reporters.

Hundreds of supporters camped outside the headquarters for the duration and chanted "Megawati will win" when she emerged. Riot police, wearing wearing protective pads on their torsos and shins for the first time, stood guard but there was no violence.
Megawati was ousted as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) by a government-supported rival in June last year.
A police-backed raid on PDI headquarters sparked riots in Jakarta on July 27. At least five people died in the riots, the worst in the capital in more than two decades.
